Three endpoints landed. POST /work-items/{id}/retry { steer? } deletes the breached retry_counters row (a retry is a fresh budget, not a continuation of the exhausted one), flips the item back to active, emits work_item_retried, and re-runs from the capped node; the steer is prepended to cycle 1's fix prompt only, and only on the node the retry restarted. 409 on a node with no fix loop or an item that is not stopped. POST /documents/{id}/open { editor? } launches code/cursor/zed/obsidian or the OS default on the document's absolute path, 400 on an unknown editor id, 404 on an unknown document, and 501 when nothing on the server can open a window so the SPA falls back to vscode://file/. GET /worker-sessions/{id}/log gains ?format=jsonl returning { n, t, src, text } per line (src classified sys/stdout/agent/tool in the new src/kraft/logs.py) and ?follow=1 for an SSE tail that drains one extra poll after the session leaves running so no line is dropped; the plain-text response is unchanged for copy. 12 new tests, 243 backend tests pass, ruff clean. Gap filed: log lines carry no timestamps (Kraft-7z6.19) because the adapter gives the child an fd - t is null for ordinary stdout. Deviation: preferred_editor reads from the request body or KRAFT_EDITOR rather than a config file; the config file for it arrives with the Settings work (API-4).

Pause / steer / resume implemented per 02 §10.2, and the paused card (4c) wired to it, closing UI-4. There is no stdin into a one-shot agent CLI, so the three are one mechanism: kill this attempt, carry new context into the next. Schema v5 adds 'paused' to the work_items status CHECK and a pending_steer_context column - SQLite cannot alter a constraint, so migration 4 does the documented 12-step table rebuild with foreign keys off around it, and a test proves the rows and the events FK survive. POST /pause SIGTERMs the process group of every running session on the current node (sessions are group leaders, so an agent CLI's own children go too), marking the rows paused *before* signalling so the adapter's exit does not re-resolve them as failures; session_exited now refuses to overwrite a paused row and run_task returns 'paused'. POST /steer stores the note while paused; POST /resume relaunches the node from its current index, does not touch retry_counters, and hands the note to the executor. The note is a one-shot Steer object carried down the walk and consumed by the first agent launch, which is what both entry points - resume and retry-after-cap - actually mean by it. Frontend: Pause shows 'Pausing…' until worker_session_paused lands, the paused card prefills the note the server already holds and offers 'Resume with steer' / 'Resume without', and the store handles pause_requested, worker_session_paused, steer_context_set, work_item_resumed and work_item_retried. 253 backend + 127 frontend tests pass, ruff and tsc clean. Steer is still disabled rather than hidden on non-steerable hooks - that needs the registry's interactive flag (Kraft-7z6.14).

Closed alongside API-4. (1) Session logs now carry timestamps: the subprocess adapter gives the child a pipe instead of a file descriptor and a daemon drain thread copies the output to the log byte for byte while stamping each line into a <session>.times.jsonl sidecar. The plain-text log stays verbatim, so copy and the agent-envelope parser are untouched, and a dedicated reader means the pipe can never fill and block the child. A log with no sidecar - an adopted session, or one written before this - reads back with blank times rather than invented ones. (2) Open worktree: GET /work-items/{id} exposes worktree_path and POST /work-items/{id}/open-worktree launches an editor on it, sharing the launcher with /documents/{id}/open. (3) GET /beads/search is a thin live 'bd search --json' passthrough for the search overlay's footer strip.

Settings API landed, YAML-backed. New src/kraft/config.py does atomic read/write (temp file + os.replace, so a crash mid-save cannot leave a half-written policy) plus a read-only repo probe that reports branch, submodules from .gitmodules, beads export flags, a detected test command and the GitLab project from the remote - it never edits repo files, which is what design 5a promises. Endpoints: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /repos + POST /repos/probe (repos.yaml); GET/PUT /templates/{id} + POST /templates/{id}/validate, which writes the candidate to a scratch dir and runs the real load_templates over it rather than re-deriving the rules; GET/PUT /registry, which re-runs the chain validator across every template on save and returns what broke; GET/PUT /policy, validated through load_policy before it lands; GET/PUT /access and GET/DELETE /sessions. New src/kraft/auth.py: scrypt password hashing with a per-password salt, session cookies whose 256-bit token is stored only as a SHA-256 (a leaked DB cannot be replayed as a login), constant-time comparison, HttpOnly SameSite=lax cookies, and schema v6's auth_sessions table. Auth is off on loopback and on for anything else, per design 5e; binding off localhost with no password is refused rather than quietly allowed, and changing the password revokes every session. __main__ reads bind and port from access.yaml so 'takes effect on restart' is literally true. 17 new tests, 274 backend tests pass, ruff clean.

Login (1m): centred 300px column over the section radial, password field, Sign in, session-cookie footnote; api.ts raises one kraft:unauthenticated event on any 401 so App decides the login screen in one place, and /health stays public so the screen can name the bind address it is asking about. Settings shell + all five pages in views/Settings.tsx: Repos (5a) with an add dialog that probes as the path is typed and only enables Connect once the probe lands, destructive actions behind the overflow; Chain templates (5b) with a draft editor, Validate that reports per-repo resolvability without saving, and a save that is refused unless the draft parses; Plugins (5c) with the steerable switch bound to the registry's interactive flag and a save that names the templates it broke; Policy (5d) editing every cap together; Access (5e) with bind radios, password, session expiry and a revocable session list. Cross-repo: schema v7 adds submodules and root_merge_policy to work_items, POST /work-items accepts them, GET /work-items/{id} returns a repos array ordered deepest-submodule-first (a submodule has to merge before the parent that points at it), the detail renders the 3a repos panel and a '+N submodules' tag on multi-repo items only, and intake's collapsed 'Advanced · cross-repo' disclosure appears only when the repo's own .gitmodules actually has submodules.
